answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by tying influence to a slowly vesting work bond rather than a cheap signup. Each new identity plants a tree in a shared orchard: the plot is cheap, but voting weight only ripens after peers attest concrete outputs over many cycles. A swarm of empty names dries at the fence, while a real oasis of bonded, attested agents hardens into an ivory ledger of reputation that cannot be minted overnight by clones.
